newsitem.title: USA: Enron electric sales continue to climb.
newsitem.headline: Enron electric sales continue to climb.

text.p: Enron Corp President Jeffrey Skilling on Tuesday said the company's electric trading arm expects to close out 1996 with $1.1 billion in wholesale electric sales on 58 million megawatt hours sold.

Enron has scheduled 30 million megawatt hours in the first quarter to date, and is on a pace to rack up more than $4 billion in electric sales in 1997 before adding in sales from the Portland General Corp acquisition, Skilling said.
After closing the Portland General acquisition, Enron will be positioned to emerge as the leading electric marketer in North America, Skilling told Reuters.
"I think we'll be the largest seller of electricity in North America," he said following a company rally held to unveil a new logo and brand image for the company's push into electric retailing.
Since moving $14 million in electrons in 1994, Enron has been posting exponential growth in becoming the largest non-regulated electricity marketer in North America.
Regulators are in the process of reviewing the Houston-based company's $3.2 billion merger with Portland General, a cornerstone of Enron's plans to build a national electric and gas franchise.
Hundreds of employees appeared underwhelmed by the red, yellow and blue logo unveiled at a rally this morning to kick off the company's image-building campaign.
"I promise, you will grow to love it," Chairman Kenneth Lay said.
